title: INT8 weight-only sensitivity & canary plumbing — convergence audit and chaos harness
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Goal: Add a robust integration + regression pipeline that validates INT8 weight-only GPTQ/AWQ profiles against accuracy, stability, and latency SLO regressions before rolling to production. This ticket wires together a canary plumbing flow, sensitivity sweeps, chaos injection, and automated rollback criteria so we can safely deploy new weight-only profiles across hosted and Dedicated fleets.

Background: We've had intermittent drift after weight-only profile rollouts where rare inflation of perplexity or token-level hallucinations slipped past unit guards (see incident notes in the Confluence doc). Current regression checks are single-run smoke tests that miss cross-seed sensitivity and kernel scheduling edge cases.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Canary plumbing: tie profile registry -> canary routing policy -> telemetry gate. Implement middleware that marks requests for canary variants and tags traces for per-seed accuracy delta.
- Sensitivity sweeps: orchestrate deterministic multi-seed calibration runs (5 seeds, n=1000 prompts) across GPTQ and AWQ profile variants; collect metrics (EM, F1-like QA score, KL-divergence of logits, token-level edit distance).
- Regression harness: add nightly and PR-driven smoke suites that compare new profiles to baseline on the curated regression set (regset-v4).
- Chaos harness: GPU preemption, kernel-sched delay injection, and KV-cache eviction scenarios to expose non-deterministic stability regressions.
- Rollout policy: implement automatic rollback triggers (accuracy delta > 1.5% absolute on regset or p95 latency regression > 20% or error-rate spike > 0.5%) with optional manual override.
- Observability: dashboards and alerts (per-profile accuracy deltas, canary conversion rate, trace samples) and a runbook for on-call.

Acceptance criteria:
- Canary plumbing deployed to a non-prod canary pool and tested end-to-end.
- Sensitivity sweep job runs produce reproducible reports in S3 and add entries to the profile registry with pass/fail verdicts.
- Regression suite integrated with PR checks; any profile change that fails CI blocks merge.
- Chaos scenarios run in staging with documented failures and mitigation notes.
- Rollout policy wired to the Console so rollouts show status and can auto-rollback on threshold breaches.

Trade-offs and decisions so far:
- We chose deterministic few-seed sweeps (5 seeds) to balance compute cost with statistical coverage; larger sweeps will be a follow-up if we see high variance.
- Metric selection favors relative accuracy (EM/F1) and KL on logits rather than raw perplexity because perplexity alone was a noisy indicator in previous rollouts.
- Initial rollout will gate only weight-only INT8 profiles; FP8 remains out of scope for now to reduce combinatorial testing.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Build the canary request tagging middleware and extend the routing layer to respect profile annotations (owner: Marco Ruiz).
2) Extend calibration runner to parameterize seeds and profile variants and emit standardized report JSON (owner: Priya Patel).
3) Add regression suite entries and PR-harness integration (owner: SLO team contributor: Ava Chen).
4) Implement chaos experiments using the staging chaos runner and schedule a 48h focused run (owner: Reliability: Jordan Lee).
5) Wire metrics to Console and create dashboards/alerts (owner: Observability: Lina Gomez).

Links & artifacts:
- Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/INT8+Weight-Only+Rollout+Playbook (design + incident notes)
- PR for canary middleware: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4398
- Calibration runner prototype: https://github.com/redwood-inference/calibration/compare/feature/sensitivity-sweeps
- Regression set (regset-v4) S3 bucket: s3://redwood-regtests/regset-v4
- Draft runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/INT8+Canary+Runbook

Notes on compute budget and cost controls:
- To contain costs, sweep jobs run on preemptible GPU nodes with a max runtime cap of 4h; longer runs will bequeued to reserved capacity.
- Results are cached by profile hash to avoid recomputing identical calibration outputs.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: AWQ variants show higher variance across seeds. Mitigation: require AWQ candidates to pass an expanded 10-seed sensitivity test before canary.
- Risk: Chaos tests may destabilize shared staging; mitigation: run chaos in isolated GPU pools and schedule during low-traffic windows.

Next steps (short term):
- Merge canary middleware PR and deploy to staging (owner: Marco Ruiz) — target 2025-02-18.
- Run initial 5-seed sensitivity sweep for three recent candidate profiles and capture reports (owner: Priya Patel) — target 2025-02-20.
- Create initial dashboards and low-severity alerts for expected variance (owner: Lina Gomez) — target 2025-02-21.
